verdictBasis: ACCEPT at 0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX. The succession is honest at the byte level: nothing removed, no silent path, no reordering, every changed and added path covered by the closed roster, and the four digests in the LIVE remasurement block verified against the live tree at the declared HEAD. The two verbatim carries, the DR-126 register row and the six file 04 TCB lines, match their live sources exactly. Both v46 pins are hash-accurate and their verdicts, finding rosters and grade rulings are reported without embellishment. The one substantive edit, the macos-product-build landing, adds only grammar: a named observation interface, a named near-neighbour exclusion, a refusal rule, a named normalization, a canonicalIdentifier object and a closed notAdmitted. It introduces no selector value, no Apple key that is not in the recorded bytes it names and pins, no identifier, no table row, and no schemeId it would have had to mint. The three advisories are honesty and traceability observations; none of them names a byte the candidate must change.

gradeRuling.reservationSweepAttestation: My verdict carries no reservation-language sentence. I swept my own advisories, verdictBasis and reasons for conditional grants, exception clauses, and any sentence of the form 'a byte must change before an unreserved grant'. There are none. Each advisory states in its own notAFinding line that it does not reserve this grant, and none of the three is conditioned on the grade.
reasons: The single ground on which I ruled NOT SUSTAINED at v46 is discharged in the bytes. That ruling rested entirely on macos-product-build carrying no named source interface, no near-neighbour exclusion and no absent/unobservable refusal rule, while every sibling selector branch carried all three. The subject now supplies all three, and adds the named normalization and the canonicalIdentifier object that EXACT-BUILD.equality's phrase 'after that scheme's named normalization' presupposes. My v46 reservation was confined by its own terms to that one path, and that path is the one this successor edited.

The load-bearing defect I identified is gone. supportedVersionOrBuildSelector.serialization binds the later packet with 'The later packet chooses values inside this language and MUST NOT mint range or scheme semantics.' At v46 a packet author populating the macOS profile had to decide which interface produced the token, which is scheme semantics the grammar forbade them to mint. At v47 the grammar makes that decision for them: the interface is the sw_vers observation CLI family, the near neighbour sw_vers -productVersion is excluded by name, uname is excluded by name, no second form is admitted, and the observation refuses when the string is unobservable, missing or empty. The author now selects a value inside a closed language rather than minting semantics.

The designation is determinate rather than merely present. Within the named CLI family the two candidate strings are the product version and the product build string; the grammar excludes the first by name and designates the second, leaving one referent. Equality is then closed end to end: normalization is NFC plus trim with no case-fold, serialization is that normalized string, equality is byte-exact after that serialization, wildcardRejected and emptyRejected hold at the EXACT-BUILD tag, noOrJoin forbids alternatives, and schemeBinding confines the scheme to osFamily=macos. Both members of osFamilyEnum now compare determinately.

The macOS refusal rule is at or above the standard its siblings set, not below it. It refuses on unobservable, missing, or empty after normalization, which is broader than the Linux sibling's 'If VERSION_ID is absent the profile refuses', and it names the substitute it will not accept. Ambiguity has no branch because the named family emits one product-build string, whereas the filesystem member needs an ambiguity branch because its Linux interface can.

The two remaining asymmetries with linux-distro-userspace are not bytes this candidate needs. macos-product-build carries no schemeId, but no rule in the grammar consumes one: EXACT-BUILD.requires an identifierScheme from identifierSchemes, which is the map key, schemeBinding addresses both schemes by map key, and comparisonAlgorithm opensip-platform-build-exact.1 sits at the tag level and covers both. And the field inside the CLI output is designated semantically rather than by Apple key name, which is the correct choice, since minting ProductBuildVersion would be inventing an unrecorded key and would be the graver defect.

The grant's scope is met on its own terms. What is graded is the selector grammar precisely while values and per-OS profiles stay RESERVED, and I verified that they do: all four slice1ProfileStems keep both required members at standing RESERVED, identityRuleShape.populatedTables stays RESERVED as G22 qualification evidence, and no table row exists. An unreserved application-grade grant here asserts that a population packet can be built against this grammar without inventing anything, and for both osFamily values that is now true.

Nothing outside the grammar contradicts the grant. Every digest the subject pins verifies against the live tree at the declared HEAD, both verbatim carries match their sources byte for byte, both round pins are hash-accurate and honestly reported, the delta is fully covered by the closed roster with nothing removed and nothing reordered, and status, binds, reviewStatus and sealRecommendation all hold at their reserved values. I found no byte of this subject that would need to change before the grant.

My three advisories are citation standing, roster over-inclusion, and a carried pre-v6 standing gap. None of them names a byte that must change, none is a defect in the selector grammar, and each is repairable on a later round without touching the grammar at all. I record them as honesty work and not as a reservation.
